key_insight: MGE-PO improves mathematical reasoning by shaping policy advantages with both correctness and rollout entropy, giving low-entropy correct answers bigger rewards and high-entropy wrong answers bigger penalties.
engineering_relevance: The method adds a practical entropy-aware credit assignment rule that can be plugged into policy optimization to better exploit confidence signals during training.
method: 4Q advantage shaping combines verified correctness with generation entropy to set the sign and size of credit adjustments.
Lower-entropy successes get larger positive bonuses; higher-entropy failures get larger negative penalties.
An online entropy-based curriculum uses cached rollout measurements to prioritize training questions.
evidence_signal: After eight epochs, the 4Q augmentation improved six-benchmark macro avg@32 by 3.23-3.69% and macro pass@32 by 4.24-11.06% on Qwen3-8B-Base, and raised Qwen2.5-7B-Base four-benchmark macro avg@32 from 41.5% to 45.4%.
watch_item: The approach depends on reliable entropy estimates from cached rollouts, so its gains may be sensitive to rollout quality, entropy calibration, and training setup.
paper_title: MGE-PO: Entropy-Aware Credit Assignment for Mathematical Reasoning
